versions.provenance: 8th edition (and FIGO where applicable) endometrial carcinoma staging, rewritten from criteria published on Medscape/public references; interim content pending the licensed content and R1 clinical verification.
versions.introduction:
8th edition staging of endometrial carcinoma covers carcinomas of the uterine corpus (and carcinosarcoma, staged as carcinoma) and corresponds to the FIGO 2009 surgical staging system, so each T category maps to a FIGO stage (shown in the labels). Uterine sarcomas such as leiomyosarcoma and endometrial stromal sarcoma are staged with separate systems.

Stage grouping is anatomic and rests on surgical-pathologic assessment of myometrial invasion, cervical stromal involvement, and extrauterine and nodal spread, with nodal disease subdivided into pelvic (IIIC1) and para-aortic (IIIC2). The key nuance is that, although stage is anatomic, FIGO histologic grade (1 to 3) and histologic type strongly influence prognosis and management: serous, clear cell, and undifferentiated carcinomas and carcinosarcoma are treated as high risk, and molecular classification (POLE-mutated, MMR-deficient, p53-abnormal, no specific molecular profile) increasingly guides care.

t.label: T1 (FIGO I): Tumor confined to the corpus uteri, including endocervical glandular involvement
T1a (FIGO IA): Tumor limited to the endometrium or invading less than one half of the myometrium
T1b (FIGO IB): Tumor invades one half or more of the myometrium
T2 (FIGO II): Tumor invades the stromal connective tissue of the cervix but does not extend beyond the uterus (endocervical glandular involvement alone is T1, not T2)
T3 (FIGO III): Tumor involves the serosa, adnexa, vagina, or parametrium (local and/or regional spread)
T3a (FIGO IIIA): Tumor involves the serosa of the corpus uteri and/or the adnexa (by direct extension or metastasis)
T3b (FIGO IIIB): Vaginal involvement (by direct extension or metastasis) or parametrial involvement
T4 (FIGO IVA): Tumor invades the bladder mucosa and/or the bowel mucosa (bullous edema alone does not qualify as T4)

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
Isolated tumor cells in regional lymph node(s) no larger than 0.2 mm
N1 (FIGO IIIC1): Regional lymph node metastasis to pelvic lymph nodes
N1mi: Pelvic lymph node metastasis measuring > 0.2 mm and <= 2.0 mm in greatest dimension
N1a: Pelvic lymph node metastasis measuring > 2.0 mm in greatest dimension
N2 (FIGO IIIC2): Regional lymph node metastasis to para-aortic lymph nodes, with or without positive pelvic lymph nodes
N2mi: Para-aortic lymph node metastasis measuring > 0.2 mm and <= 2.0 mm in greatest dimension, with or without positive pelvic nodes
N2a: Para-aortic lymph node metastasis measuring > 2.0 mm in greatest dimension, with or without positive pelvic nodes

m.label: M1 (FIGO IVB): Distant metastasis, including metastasis to inguinal lymph nodes, intraperitoneal disease, or spread to lung, liver, or bone. It excludes metastasis to para-aortic or pelvic nodes, the vagina, the pelvic serosa, or the adnexa.

stageGroups.basis: Tumor limited to endometrium or < half myometrial invasion, node-negative.
Invasion of half or more of the myometrium, node-negative.
Cervical stromal invasion without extrauterine spread, node-negative.
Metastasis to para-aortic lymph nodes, with or without positive pelvic nodes.
Invasion of bladder and/or bowel mucosa.
Distant metastasis, including intra-abdominal spread and/or inguinal node involvement.

versions.regionalNodes: Regional lymph nodes are the pelvic nodes (paracervical, parametrial, hypogastric [obturator, internal iliac], external iliac, common iliac, presacral) and the para-aortic nodes. Para-aortic involvement is regional (FIGO IIIC2).
versions.histologicGrade: FIGO grade for endometrioid carcinoma is based on the proportion of solid, nonsquamous/nonmorular growth: G1 <= 5%, G2 6% to 50%, G3 > 50%. Marked nuclear atypia inappropriate for the architectural grade raises the grade by one. Serous, clear cell, and undifferentiated carcinomas are regarded as high grade by definition.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Endometrioid adenocarcinoma (and its variants) is the most common. Higher-risk types include serous carcinoma, clear cell carcinoma, mixed carcinoma, undifferentiated/dedifferentiated carcinoma, mucinous carcinoma, and carcinosarcoma (staged as carcinoma).
prognosticFactors: FIGO stage (depth of myometrial invasion, cervical, adnexal, and nodal spread)
Histologic type (serous, clear cell, undifferentiated, and carcinosarcoma are high risk)
Regional lymph node status (pelvic vs para-aortic)
Peritoneal cytology and molecular subtype (POLE-mutated, MMR-deficient, p53-abnormal, no specific molecular profile)
